findings.message: The nightly `time.proposal-hours-refresh` workflow is the round-4 fix for proposals that had hours before 104: their `waiting_hours` starts at 0 and no event refills it. No test runs this workflow. `schedules.test.ts` only checks that the cron entry is listed. If the workflow failed to fill `waiting_hours`, every test would still pass. Add a table-driven test that runs the workflow through the engine or `run()` over at least three cases: approved-only hours, hours in a submitted week, and a project whose entries were all deleted. Each case should check `delivery.proposal.hours` and `waiting_hours` afterwards.
findings.scenario: Hours logged on CON-014 before migration 0022, in a submitted week → after deploy the Time card shows no waiting line until some entry or week event fires. If the workflow's query or step were broken, no test would fail.

findings.message: The cron is declared with `timezone: "entity"`, so it is scheduled once per legal entity. Each run still recomputes every project in the tenant (`select distinct project_id from time.entry …`). A tenant with N entities does the same full refresh N times a night. Either schedule it per tenant, or limit each run to the projects whose entries belong to that entity's people.
findings.scenario: A tenant with LK and AU entities → two identical full-tenant refreshes at 02:30 local in each zone.

findings.message: A push that only drafts hours (no proposal created, updated or withdrawn) has `listed` false. It returns `outcome: "unchanged"` and writes no `delivery.sync_push` row, even though it wrote `commit_day_draft` and ledger rows and emitted `delivery.commit.time` events. `pushRow` also never stores `drafted`, `unlinked` or `unverified`, so the Repo sync card can't show why a person got suggestions. Count `drafted > 0` as a change, or persist the counts.
findings.scenario: CI pushes main after a day of work on FLT-101 with no phase change → result `unchanged`, but 3 timesheet suggestions appear and the Repo sync card shows nothing.

findings.message: The README says "A draft says who pushed it". After round 4, the suggestion only says "From your own sync" or "Sent by someone else's sync (CI or another person)", and never names the pusher (`suggestions.ts`). Reword it to match the code.

The README says the info tooltip shows "on hover and keyboard focus". `AgentFirstLine` opens it on hover, click or Enter (popover target). Keyboard focus alone doesn't open it. Either make the docs match the click/Enter behaviour, or add an `onFocus` open.
findings.scenario: Tab to the info icon → nothing shows until Enter is pressed, contrary to the README.

findings.message: The e2e assertions for the hours figure, the agents lede and the "Where time went" legend were loosened or removed instead of pinned. The cause: Time's new `currentWeek` uses the real date through `localToday`, while Delivery's push uses the tenant's `clock_pin` (`clockOf`). So the pinned e2e tenant now opens on an empty week. That leaves two notions of "today" in one change, and the Overview test no longer checks the figures. Either let `currentWeek` honour the tenant clock, or pin the clock in the e2e test and restore the exact assertions.
findings.scenario: e2e tenant pinned to 2026-10-16 → Overview shows the real current week at 0 h; the test passes with any number.

findings.message: `waiting()` still applies a limit before the approver filter: it takes the newest 52 distinct submitted weeks, then calls `teamWeek` for each. That can mean up to 52 separate read transactions on every Overview load. A week older than the scan window that waits on this viewer silently drops off, with no sign that the list was cut short. Filter by the viewer's approvable weeks in SQL, or flag the list as partial when the scan was exhausted.
findings.scenario: A large tenant with submitted weeks in each of the last 52 ISO weeks for other approvers, and one older week waiting on Maya → Maya's Overview omits it with no partial marker.

findings.message: `commits: z.array(CommitInput).max(2000)` is checked per record, but the reader caps only the whole repo walk (20,000). One change with more than 2000 named commits makes `PushInput.parse` throw, so the whole push fails and no proposal syncs. Either cap or truncate in the reader and send no `commits` when it is over the limit ("not read"), or raise the limit to match.
findings.scenario: A long-running change with 2,100 `specclaw(NNN-x)` commits → sync_specclaw throws a validation error; no proposals in the project sync.

findings.message: The production path never applies the cross-midnight rule in `sync/estimate.ts`. `byDay` splits a person's commits by local day before they reach the ledger, and the ledger keys rows on (person, proposal, day). `dayHours` then runs `estimateDays` over one day's commits only. So a session that crosses midnight becomes two separate sessions, and each one gets its own 30-minute lead-in. The rule that splits a session at midnight, and the rule that moves the lead-in to the first commit's day, both live only in the table test, so the documented rule and the drafted figure disagree. Fix: make `dayHours` estimate over this day's ledger plus the adjacent days' ledgers (or over a window around the day), then take that day's slice. Add a DB test that crosses midnight and goes through `draftSyncTime`.
findings.scenario: UTC person, own sync carries commit A at 2026-11-12T23:30Z and commit B at 2026-11-13T00:45Z. The README and `estimate.ts` rule gives one session, 23:00→00:45: 1 h on Nov 12 and 0.75 h on Nov 13. The sync instead drafts 0.5 h on Nov 12 (23:00–23:30) and 0.5 h on Nov 13 (00:15–00:45), 1 h in total instead of 1.75 h.

findings.message: `dismissRepoDraft` marks only commits still marked `by === "ci"` as dismissed. `merge` has already relabelled to `"own"` any commit that the person's own sync confirmed after CI drafted it, and it added nothing for that commit, because the CI draft's hours already counted as suggested. Dismissing the CI draft then removes its hours from `suggestedHours`, but those commits stay in the estimate as `own`. Nothing re-drafts them: `draftDay` returns early when `added` is empty, and later own syncs see `by: "own"` and add nothing. The person's own work is lost for good, which contradicts the doc line "the person's own sync can bring them back". Meanwhile the CI suggestion still says "Sent by someone else's sync … dismiss it if it isn't your work". Fix: when dismissing, re-draft the day for commits already confirmed `own` (draft the estimate minus the remaining suggested hours, as a trusted draft), or count the CI draft as trusted once the own sync confirms its commits.
findings.scenario: CI pushes Nimal's commit A on Nov 10 and Time shows an untrusted 0.5 h suggestion. Nimal's own sync then carries A: `merge` relabels it `own`, adds nothing, drafts nothing. Nimal dismisses the CI suggestion, so `dismissed_at` is set and suggested drops to 0. Later own syncs carry A again: `e.by === "own"`, nothing is added, nothing is drafted. Nimal's 0.5 h never comes back.

findings.message: The "each commit once, whichever path" claim is keyed per proposal. The webhook files a commit under the proposal its task line names (`tasks[0].key`). The sync files it under the proposal of the change folder in its subject. Nothing on the sync path checks `delivery.commit_draft`, the per-commit claim the webhook still writes. When the two keys differ, both paths draft the same commit. Fix: make the per-commit claim independent of the proposal. For example, check `commit_draft` (person + sha) in `merge`/`draftDay`, or key the hook entry by person and sha across proposals.
findings.scenario: Commit `specclaw(101-export): T1` whose body says `CON-014 T3 done` and `Time: 1h`. The webhook drafts 1 h on CON-014 for the day. Nimal's sync then carries the same sha under FLT-101, finds an empty ledger row for FLT-101 that day, and drafts another 0.5 h. One commit ends up with two suggestions.
